messages:
maria: Heads up — ran into a weird tie/oscillation case in the policy engine when region weights are effectively equal. Seen in canary: requests flip between us-east/us-west every few minutes and latency oscillates.
aj: I saw this too. Tie-breaker is deterministic on route id which biases one region. When probe latencies jitter it causes flip-flop.
kevin: Impact: a customer experienced 2x p50 during the flip period. We should avoid pathological switching.
jun: Product note — customers want fairness across regions and tenants; we can’t silently move them around for cost wins if it worsens latency.
sam: Quick idea: use probe_score (recent probe RTT) + EWMA smoothing and a small randomized tie-break to prevent determinism.
maria: Proposal sketch:
- add probe_score into policy eval inputs
- introduce TIE_EPSILON and if scores within epsilon use weighted_random over softmax(scores)
- add temporal dampening (decay) to prevent rapid flipping
- expose tunables per-tenant

aj: Implementation question: policy eval currently returns a single route_score number. Do we change the contract to return a score_breakdown (cost, latency, probe) or keep opaque and emit probe as side telemetry?
kevin: Ops prefers non-breaking. Emitting telemetry from sidecar avoids immediate contract change but loses atomicity for rollouts.
sam: We can version the policy proto (v2 includes score_breakdown). Runtime can fallback to v1 semantics if it sees v1 policy — migration path.
maria: I lean toward expanding the contract (score_breakdown). It helps explainability and will be useful in Console and Optimize.
aj: Concern: weighted-random tie-break may increase long-tail latency if we send some traffic to marginally worse routes. Need a tunable PROBE_WEIGHT and guardrail: only randomize when delta < TIE_EPSILON and score variance low.
kevin: Ops asks for metrics: tie_count, route_flip_rate, per-route probe_ewma, and SLA-violation-rate after change.
sam: Pseudocode (brain-dump):

```
score = base_score - cost_penalty - latency_penalty
score += probe_score * PROBE_WEIGHT
if abs(score[a] - score[b]) < TIE_EPSILON:
    winner = weighted_random(routes, weights=softmax(score))
else:
    winner = argmax(score)
```

aj: Interface boundary question: should policy engine be authoritative (return final winner) or should it return candidate list + scores and let runtime choose? That affects testing surface.
maria: Prefer policy to return candidate list + score_breakdown. Keeps runtime simple and makes policy testable. Runtime can implement safe-guard heuristics (max consecutive flips) too.
kevin: We'll need a sim-run before rollout. I can run the route-sim harness for 48h with production-like jitter and measure flip rate and p95 impact.
sam: I’ll write an RFC today with proto v2, migration plan, and guardrail configs (TIE_EPSILON, PROBE_WEIGHT, DECAY_HALF_LIFE). Will include a non-breaking feature flag path.
jun: Console needs an explainer panel: show per-route probe EWMA and flip events for tenants. Can we add a telemetry tag so Console shows it without proto changes? ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed policy-v2 to us-east-1 for 5% traffic :rocket:
aj: Add tests: deterministic replay with fixed RNG seed, and seeding behavior when weighted_random used. Also unit tests for EWMA smoothing and decay.
maria: Risks: weighted-random can increase tail if mis-tuned; adding probe_score increases dependency on probe health (need probe health checks); expanding proto is a breaking surface if we don’t version it.
kevin: Action items: run sim (kevin), draft RFC (sam), add unit tests + seed control (aj), add canary watch and metrics (ops). I’ll start sim tonight and post results.
sam: Will include rollout: v2 opt-in flag per-tenant, automatic rollback if flip_rate > threshold or p95 worsens by > X%.
jun: Decision timeline: want to pick approach by EOW. Tagging owners above.
ops-bot: monitor-bot: started watch on canary, alerting on flip_rate > 0.5% or p95 delta > 20%.
maria: Thanks all — collecting notes. Sam, Kevin, Aj — ping me when you have sim/RFC/tests. I’ll follow up with a short architecture follow-up doc.
